title: Enable GitHub security enforcement
summary: Enable supported GitHub secret scanning, push protection, and immutable Action SHA enforcement, and publish annotated governance recovery tags without moving branches.
reason: The security inventory found repository secret scanning disabled and Action SHA pinning unenforced despite all checked-in workflows already using immutable references; the prior governance rollback plan also lacked named recovery refs.
behavior_before: GitHub secret scanning and push protection were disabled, Action references were not required to use full SHAs, and rollback commits were documented but had no annotated remote recovery tags.
behavior_after: GitHub secret scanning and push protection are enabled, Actions require full commit SHA references, and annotated remote tags preserve the pre-governance main tip and normalized baseline.
manual_validation: PASS: repository security_and_analysis reports secret_scanning=enabled and secret_scanning_push_protection=enabled.
PASS: repository Actions permissions report sha_pinning_required=true; checked-in workflow audit found no non-SHA uses references.
PASS: secret-scanning open-alert query returned zero findings after enablement.
rollback_plan: Do not move or delete the recovery tags during ordinary rollback. If the strengthened GitHub settings cause an evidenced platform incompatibility, change only the specific repository setting through a separately reviewed governance action; never weaken checked-in Action pins.
notes: GitHub accepted base secret scanning and push protection. Non-provider patterns and validity checks remain disabled because the repository API did not enable those advanced surfaces. No alert was dismissed, no branch moved, and no required check was changed.
